title: The Atonement of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The atonement of Christ is His saving work by which He deals with sin, guilt, judgment, wrath, reconciliation, and peace with God. Through His death, sinners are cleansed, forgiven, and brought near.
summary: The atonement of Christ is His saving work by which He deals with sin, guilt, judgment, wrath, reconciliation, and peace with God. Through His death, sinners are cleansed, forgiven, and brought near.
christFocus: Jesus is the Lamb of God who takes away sin. His atoning death reveals God’s justice, mercy, love, and grace as He gives Himself to save sinners.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Sin creates real guilt before the holy God. Atonement is necessary because sinners cannot remove their own sin, satisfy divine justice, or reconcile themselves to God.

The atonement of Christ is centered in His sacrificial death. Jesus gives Himself as the offering for sin, bearing judgment, cleansing guilt, and opening the way for forgiveness.

At the cross, God is shown to be both just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus. Sin is not ignored, and mercy is not cheap. Justice and grace meet in Christ.

The atonement is sufficient because of who Christ is. The eternal Son became man and offered Himself without blemish, securing redemption that sinners could never achieve.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Without atonement, people are left with religious effort, shame management, denial, or despair. The Bible gives something greater: Christ has dealt with sin at its deepest level.

This doctrine keeps the Gospel from becoming vague love or moral inspiration. God saves through the blood of His Son, and that saving work brings peace to the guilty.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to God through the atoning work of Christ. Do not minimize your sin or try to atone for yourself through suffering, good deeds, or self-punishment. Trust the sacrifice God has provided and worship the Savior who made peace by His blood.
